pr_body:
![editor_scrollbars](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/76c26776-8fe4-47f8-9c79-9add7d7d2151)

Closes #4427 

Release Notes:

- Added a horizontal scrollbar to the editor panel
- Added `axis` option to `scrollbar` in the Zed configuration, which can forcefully disable either the horizontal or vertical scrollbar
- Added `horizontal_scroll_margin` equivalent to `vertical_scroll_margin` in the Zed configuration

Rough Edges:

This feature seems mostly stable from my testing. I've been using a development build for about a week with no issues. Any feedback would be appreciated. There are a few things to note as well:

1. Scrolling to the lower right occasionally causes scrollbar clipping on my end, but it isn't consistent and it isn't major. Some more testing would definitely be a good idea. [FIXED]
2. Documentation may need to be modified
3. I added an `AxisPair` type to the `editor` crate to manage values that have a horizontal and vertical variant. I'm not sure if that's the optimal way to do it, but I didn't see a good alternative. The `Point` type would technically work, but it may cause confusion.
pr_comments: We require contributors to sign our Contributor License Agreement, and we don't have @frqubit on file. You can sign our CLA at https://zed.dev/cla. Once you've signed, post a comment here that says '@cla-bot check'.
The cla-bot has been summoned, and re-checked this pull request!

There's a problem with this I only recently found. There are scrollbar settings for how much extra space should be at the end (none, one space, or a full page). For some reason, the text does not accommodate a full page width in the horizontal direction, and it has issues with one line. I'm looking through that, that's what's causing the delay. I've also had to work on other things as well which is why this is taking so long.

It seems like the settings for the maximum scroll and the width of the scrollbar are handled in completely separate places. That seems to be the source of the problem. It is not fixed yet, but now the max scroll does obey `settings.scroll_beyond_last_line`.
As far as I know, this is working. I still need to test it with other configuration settings, but I'm having no issues with my current setup. I'll also need to test it with F11.
I've played around with your branch a bit and I'm not sold on having overscroll on horizontal scrollbar; is there any benefit to it other than the consistency with vertical scrollbar?

> I've played around with your branch a bit and I'm not sold on having overscroll on horizontal scrollbar; is there any benefit to it other than the consistency with vertical scrollbar?

I don't believe so, it's mainly there for consistency. The vertical scrollbar does interfere with the text sometimes if the overscroll is not set, but that can easily be fixed by adding a bit of spacing at the end.
Yeah, we could account for the width of vertical scrollbar when calculating the width of a viewport for the horizontal scrollbar.

> I wonder if we could somehow use [Along](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/blob/77b8296fbbf2f68d2ae9bdcb04d222de3f69cd59/crates/gpui/src/geometry.rs#L38) to simplify some of this code.

We may be able to. I'll get that implemented for `AxisPair` and see where it could be useful. A lot of `AxisPair`s also use `Option`s, so that could definitely be simplified. I'm not really sure if `Along` will really fix that, but it should help it be more readable.

A few things may be simplifiable with `Along` still, particularly [`layout_scrollbars`](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/blob/3cc6d7604f89d03bcfdfaa56ec165c2221820036/crates/editor/src/element.rs#L1178). Other than that, all requested changes have been made now. The overscroll has been fixed.
I still need to add checked_div. I'll do that when I fix the merge conflict.
Awesome, I'm looking forward to see this in a release !

review_comments: Let's use something like `checked_div` here. Better safe than sorry.

These are `f32`. I don't see a way to use `checked_div` here. The division is by `text_unit_size` in every case. Looking closer it looks like `text_unit_size` could theoretically be 0 in some cases (only when the scrollbar thumb is the exact same size as the bar), but I've never seen it happen. For the sake of safety, I'll add a separate check for 0 in `layout_scrollbars` (where the value is set) and if it's 0 the scrollbar will not be drawn. The thumb would not be movable in that case anyway.

I don't see a way to do this that doesn't break the functionality. This already seems to be handled elsewhere as well, since the scrollbars do not show anyway when the thumb would take up the entire bar. I can look into this more if desired.

This division has been present for months now, and I haven't touched it to avoid breaking things. I can't guarantee that `text_unit_size` will never be 0 though.

That's fine. We can keep it as is, especially given that we're not going to do another release till early next year (which should give this code some testing time on Nightly). I suggested checking for 0 here just because there's no real precedent for it and it would make the code better IMHO, but I think we can get by.
